predictions.rationale: The retrieved file IvyNode.java is directly related to the issue as it deals with Ivy nodes, which are central to dependency resolution.
BasicResolver.java is involved in the resolution process, and changes to it could affect how dependencies are resolved, which is the root cause of the issue.
Ivy.java is the main class of Ivy, and changes to it could have a broad impact on the entire dependency resolution process.
ModuleDescriptor.java is crucial for defining and managing module metadata, which is essential for resolving dependencies.
Artifact.java defines the interface for artifacts, which are the actual files that make up a module. Changes to this interface could affect how artifacts are handled during resolution.
ArtifactId.java is used to uniquely identify artifacts. Changes to this class could affect how artifacts are referenced and resolved.
ArtifactRevisionId.java is used to uniquely identify specific revisions of artifacts. Changes to this class could affect how artifact versions are resolved.

Configuration.java defines the configurations of a module, which are used to specify which artifacts should be included in a build. Changes to this class could affect how configurations are handled during resolution.
ConflictManager.java is responsible for resolving conflicts between different versions of the same artifact. Changes to this interface could affect how conflicts are handled during resolution.
DefaultArtifact.java is a concrete implementation of the Artifact interface. Changes to this class could affect how artifacts are created and used during resolution.
